cards.title: Rare means hard to get
cards.body: Think of stickers. A plain sticker is easy to find. A shiny gold one is rare. Kids will swap many plain stickers for one gold one. Rare things are worth more swaps.

interaction.prompt: Why is the gold sticker worth more?
interaction.reveal: There are very few gold ones. When something is hard to get, people give more to get it.

cards.title: Make more, worth less
cards.body: Say a pot holds L$120 of value. All the coins share it equally. Slide to make more coins. Watch what each coin is worth.

cards.title: VAULT has a cap
cards.body: VAULT can never go past 21,000,000 coins. No more can ever be made. That keeps it rare. Tap to compare keeping the cap with making lots more.

options.label: Keep the cap
options.result: Coins stay rare, so nobody can shrink their worth by making more.

options.label: Make many more
options.result: ↓ Coins are easier to get, so each is worth less.

cards.title: Rare needs fans too
cards.body: Rare is only half the story. A rare thing nobody wants is not worth much. People must want it too. Rare and wanted together make a higher price.

interaction.prompt: Is every rare thing worth a lot?
options: No, people must also want it
interaction.explain: Worth comes from being rare and wanted. A rare thing nobody wants stays cheap.

quiz.prompt: VAULT can never go past 21,000,000 coins. What would happen if someone could suddenly make millions more?
options: Each coin would be worth more
Each coin would likely be worth less
quiz.explain: When more coins exist and the same people want them, each coin is easier to get. That makes each one worth less. The cap keeps VAULT rare.

trader.title: Spread your risk, spot the hype

cards.title: One basket is risky
cards.body: Imagine your L$1,000 sits in one coin. If that coin drops, your whole pile drops with it. This is called concentration risk. One coin carries all the weight.

interaction.prompt: What does a drop in that coin do?
interaction.reveal: All of your L$1,000 feels it. Nothing else in your pile is there to soften the fall.

cards.title: Spreading your money
cards.body: Spreading means keeping money in several places, including L$ or PEG. Slide to put more into one coin. See how much is left for everything else.

interaction.label: Share of money in one coin

cards.title: The hype cycle
cards.body: Hype is buying because everyone else is buying. A coin like ZOOMZ can climb fast this way. But the crowd moves on. Tap to see both halves of the cycle.

options.label: Crowd rushing in
options.result: ↑ Lots of buyers at once, so the price climbs fast.

options.label: Crowd moves on
options.result: ↓ Fewer new buyers arrive, so the price slides back.

cards.title: Crowds are not proof
cards.body: A busy crowd tells you people are excited. It does not tell you the coin is sound. Ask what the coin does and who holds it. Then decide how much to risk.

interaction.prompt: Everyone is buying a coin. Is that enough reason?
options: No, hype fades; check the coin itself
interaction.explain: Hype can lift a price fast and fade just as fast. The coin's idea and holders matter more.

quiz.prompt: A player puts L$900 of L$1,000 into ZOOMZ because everyone is buying it. What is the main risk?
options: Too much in one hyped coin
quiz.explain: Putting most money in one coin is concentration risk, and hype tends to fade. Spreading money across several places, including L$ or PEG, softens a fall.

cards.title: Anatomy of a launch
cards.body: Every launch has the same parts. Creators make the coins, keep a share, and open a pool with some L$. Then they promote it. Four quick checks show whether a launch could hide a rug pull.

interaction.prompt: Tap to see the four checks
interaction.reveal: Who holds the coins, is the pool locked, when do locked coins unlock, and is the volume real?

cards.title: Who holds the coins
cards.body: BLOOP's creator holds 60% of its coins. Slide the creator's share. Here we pretend all the coins together are worth L$1,000. See what the creator could dump at once.

cards.title: Locked or unlocked pool
cards.body: The pool holds the L$ and coins that people trade against. A rug pull means creators pull that money out and sell their coins. Only an unlocked pool allows it. Tap to compare.

options.label: Pool locked
options.result: Creators cannot remove the money, so a pull is blocked.

options.label: Pool unlocked
options.result: ↓ Creators can pull the pool, and holders get little back.

cards.title: The Official look-alike
cards.body: A coin with Official in its name, loud hype and an unlocked pool is a pattern. Names cost nothing to copy. Check holders and the pool lock, not the label.

interaction.prompt: A hyped coin says Official. What is the best first step?
options: Check holder share and pool lock
Join fast before the hype ends
interaction.explain: A name proves nothing. Holder share and pool lock show whether a rug pull is possible.

quiz.prompt: Which launch has the most rug pull warning signs?
options: Creator holds 60%, pool unlocked, heavy hype
Pool locked, many holders, unlocks released slowly
Small team share and a public unlock schedule
quiz.explain: A huge creator share plus an unlocked pool lets creators drain the money and sell, while hype brings in buyers. The other launches limit what creators can do.
